source.title: Discovering Millions of Interpretable Features with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xinyang He; Wei Wang; Bing Zhao; Xuan-Cheng Ren; Wen-Bo Li; Wei Qiao; Hua Wei; Lin Qu

record.tranche_reason: Measures model-loss recovery when SAE reconstructions replace activations, bearing on whether reconstruction errors affect model performance. It does not compare with random errors matched in size, as V3 requires.
record.gate_note: The paper reports activation-level FVE and model-level DLL for SAE reconstruction, including comparisons across layers, positions, dictionary sizes, and sparsity levels. Only DLL bears on V3; FVE does not measure the claimed error structure. Refusal steering and cited results are not results about dark matter.
record.test_reason: This is an SAE release paper for Qwen3-Instruct models. It reports the SAEs' own reconstruction quality (FVE) and model-performance recovery (DLL) across layers, sites, widths and L0, plus a refusal-steering demo. It never analyses the error term itself: no linear prediction of error, no per-token error scaling, and no matched-norm random-error baseline. So DLL cannot show that SAE errors are pathological (V3). Steering is never compared with or without the error term (V5), and no alternative architectures or objectives are compared (V6). The results describe the authors' SAEs, not dark matter.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present Qwen3-Instruct SAE as a resource. They report layer- and site-dependent sparsity–fidelity trade-offs, with attention SAEs recovering performance worst, and show that one selected SAE feature per model steers toward refusal. They draw no conclusions about the structure of SAE error.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates SAE reconstruction using DLL and FVE across Qwen3 models, layers, positions, dictionary sizes, and sparsity settings; it does not analyze error-vector predictability or compare reconstruction errors to matched-size random errors.
record.method_sensitivity: DLL varies by layer and SAE position; the authors also report a dictionary-size stability difference for attention SAEs and a general DLL improvement with larger target L0.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE splicing harms downstream loss far more at attention outputs than at the residual stream or MLP, with a recovery dip at layers 2–4 in Qwen3-1.7B; a similar site pattern appears in Qwen3-4B. FVE stays high where DLL is poor, so activation-level fidelity and model-level recovery diverge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The downstream loss impact of SAE reconstruction error varies strongly by activation site and depth, and is not tracked by fraction of variance explained.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger target L0 improves DLL but has little effect on FVE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-level loss recovery is more sensitive to SAE sparsity than activation-level variance explained.

record.problems: The paper provides no matched-size random-error baseline for DLL, so its results cannot test the comparative claim in V3. The reported DLL values are in figures, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. Qwen3-8B is not systematically evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: The layer-wise DLL plots contain additional per-layer values, but they are figure-only and exceed the useful level of detail for the qualitative layer patterns retained here. Activation-level FVE results were left out because they do not measure model-loss effects or any other version's named behavior.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation: not examined.
Per-token error-norm prediction across sizes, shared failure contexts, and persistence with scale: not examined (only 16K vs 65K average DLL/FVE).
Comparison of SAE-reconstruction loss impact against random errors of equal norm: not done.
Decomposition of the error into linear and nonlinear parts, and their learnability: not examined.
Whether steering or circuit analyses lose behaviour without the error term: steering adds decoder directions, with no error-term comparison.
Whether dark matter shrinks with other architectures or training objectives: only JumpReLU is trained; no architecture comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V3 tested from DLL alone, but its own notes concede there is no matched random-error baseline. That baseline is the defining comparison of V3, so I reclassify the study as T4/uses_without_test and unlink all rows. The paper's title duplicates a known title but the content is a Qwen3 SAE release. The DLL metric is not formally defined, and its plotted scale suggests fraction recovered rather than raw loss delta.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger and smaller SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
The comparison with random errors of the same size, and thus whether SAE reconstruction errors harm loss more than such random errors.
Whether the predictable component contains unlearned features and whether the nonlinear component is qualitatively different or resists further dictionary learning.
Whether analyses based on SAE features lose a meaningful share of behavior unless the error term is retained.
Whether dark matter is mainly an SAE-training artifact or shrinks with alternative architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced model activations with SAE-reconstructed activations during the forward pass and measured delta LM loss (DLL).

conditions.value: residual stream, MLP output, attention output

rows.measure: Delta LM loss (DLL), a model-performance recovery metric after replacing original activations with SAE reconstructions.
rows.note: The text says residual-stream and MLP SAEs generally recover model performance better than attention-output SAEs. The study does not compare their loss effect with matched-size random errors, so this result cannot establish V3's comparison.
rows.check: Measures loss recovery of the study's own SAEs by site. There is no random-error baseline of matched norm, so it cannot bear on V3's 'more harmful than random' comparison. Values are figure-only. The plotted DLL axis (about -0.4 to 1, higher is better) looks like fraction of loss recovered despite the name 'Delta LM loss'.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced residual-stream or MLP activations with SAE reconstructions and measured DLL by layer.
rows.note: The text reports high recovery in the first two layers, a marked decrease in layers 2–4, and gradual improvement in deeper layers. No matched-size random-error comparison is reported.
rows.check: Layer-wise recovery pattern for the study's own SAEs (dip at layers 2–4). There is no random-error control, so it bears on no version. Figure-only.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced attention-output activations with SAE reconstructions and measured DLL by layer.
rows.note: The text reports that the 65K attention SAE is less stable than the 16K SAE at the same L0, and that the layer-2 attention SAE has relatively low FVE. It does not provide a matched-size random-error comparison for DLL.
rows.check: Attention-SAE stability at 65K vs 16K width, with no random-error control. The layer-2 FVE outlier is an FVE result, not DLL. Bears on no version.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Replaced activations with SAE reconstructions and measured DLL as target L0 varied, averaging metric values across layers by position.

conditions.value: metric values averaged across all layers

rows.measure: Average DLL as a function of target L0.
rows.note: The text says a larger L0 generally leads to improved performance. This is an SAE-reconstruction comparison across sparsity settings, not a comparison with random errors of the same size.
rows.check: DLL vs target L0 averaged over layers. This is a sparsity–fidelity trade-off of the study's own SAEs, not a measure of error structure or of pathological errors.
